Chapter 10: The Question of Revolution—Can the System Be Changed?
By the end of the 1930s, the Soviet Union looked completely different than it once had. The old ruling class was gone, but in its place, a new elite had quietly stepped in.
The early promise of democracy and equality? That had faded, replaced by strict hierarchy and tight control. And for anyone still clinging to the ideals of the revolution, one question just wouldn’t go away—could this system actually change, or was it stuck in a cycle of decline?
Some people started looking back, searching for clues in the past. They remembered those first revolutionary days, when workers and peasants held real power in their own hands. This group believed the rise of the bureaucracy wasn’t some inevitable fate. It was the product of specific choices—fear, war, missed chances. So, what if ordinary people could reclaim their voice? Maybe, just maybe, the revolution could be revived.
But not everyone was so hopeful. Others saw this bureaucracy as just a new ruling class, determined to hang onto its privileges no matter what. For them, tinkering around the edges wouldn’t be enough. Real change? That would take a whole new revolution—one that truly put power back where it belonged: with the people.
Now, here’s something to think about—the possibility of change wasn’t just about politics. It was about imagination. Most folks had gotten used to the way things were. They’d adapted, learned to live within the system’s limits. The idea of genuine democracy, where everyone actually takes part? That started to feel far away, almost like a fantasy. And yet, deep down, there was still a spark—a memory that things had once been different, a quiet reminder that history isn’t set in stone.
So, the question of revolution didn’t just matter for the Soviet Union. It was about the future of socialism itself. Could a society rooted in equality and democracy really survive? Or was it always going to fall into the same old traps?
There wasn’t an easy answer. The struggle kept going. For those who just couldn’t let go of hope, the road ahead was anything but clear. There were risks, there were obstacles—plenty of both. But that dream of a better world, the dream that had once inspired millions? It was still alive, quietly waiting for its moment.
